title: Slice-wise latency/quality signal mapping for hybrid batching and KV-cache configs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Recent config rollouts (larger batching windows + more aggressive KV cache TTLs) demonstrate measurable token-cost and median-latency wins but sporadic quality regressions on some prompt slices (multi-turn dialogs and long-instruction completions). This ticket implements a repeatable, slice-aware evaluation pipeline that correlates latency quantiles with a set of quality metrics for each slice and surfaces actionable regression signals when config/model changes move us along the latency↔quality frontier.

Goals:
- Produce nightly slice-level tradeoff matrices (per config variant) mapping latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) to quality metrics (semantic-similarity AUC, exact-match on QA pairs, BLEU/ROUGE-L for seq2seq slices, hallucination rate for knowledge prompts).
- Define automated alert rules that consider both direction and magnitude (e.g., quality drop >3% on a high-traffic slice, while overall median latency improves >10%).
- Integrate results into the Console (per-route dashboard) and CI gating for config rollouts so we can prevent harmful config pushes.

Approach:
1) Slice definition: start with existing slice taxonomy (length bins, conversational-turns, instruction-vs-fewshot, code-generation) and add traffic-weight metadata. Store canonical slice set in Drive (see attachments).
2) Eval harness: extend the nightly harness to produce per-request latency traces (client+server) and map each request to a slice. Compute p50/p95/p99 latencies and lossless quality metrics.
3) Statistical testing: use paired bootstrap and Cohen's d for effect size; flag statistically significant regressions with minimum absolute thresholds to avoid noise.
4) Dashboarding & alerts: push slice-level CSVs to the Console backend and create templated Grafana panels & Alert rules. Also emit CI artifact JSON for PR gating.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive TTLs reduce cost but can hurt multi-turn coherency; larger microbatch windows improve throughput but add tail latency risk for small requests; decided to track request-size-distribution so we can attribute changes to traffic mix vs config change.

Deliverables: nightly CSVs, Console dashboard panels, PR-level artifact, alerting rules, and a short runbook for on-call triage.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly job produces a per-config, per-slice CSV with p50/p95/p99 latency and the selected quality metrics
Console has a new per-route "Slice Latency vs Quality" panel displaying heatmap and trend lines
Alerting rule created: any slice with traffic_weight > 0.01 and quality_drop >= 3% AND median_latency_improvement >= 10% triggers a P1 investigation ticket
PR gating artifact JSON is generated for every config-change PR and CI fails gated rollouts that cross configured regression thresholds
Runbook created and linked in attachments explaining triage steps and rollback policy
